title: Salt reactions - 123 school
heading: Salt reactions
intro: You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.question: What is a precipitation reaction?

answers.a: Two solutions react with each other and a solid forms
answers.b: A metal is heated until it melts
answers.d: A liquid evaporates to a gas

questions.question: What is a precipitate?

answers.a: A gas that escapes from a solution
answers.b: A liquid that floats on the water
answers.c: A solid that forms in a solution and sinks to the bottom

questions.question: How can you predict whether a precipitate forms when you mix two salt solutions?

answers.a: You check whether the formulas are the same length
answers.b: You check whether the solutions have the same colour
answers.c: You look in BINAS table 35 to see whether a combination of the ions is poorly soluble
answers.d: You check whether the solutions weigh the same

questions.question: Is AgCl very soluble or poorly soluble in water? (use BINAS table 35)
Is BaSO<sub>4</sub> very soluble or poorly soluble in water? (use BINAS table 35)
Is NaCl very soluble or poorly soluble in water? (use BINAS table 35)
Which ions always make a salt dissolve well?
What are spectator ions?

answers.c: Ions that do not take part in the reaction and stay dissolved
answers.d: Ions that disappear into the air

questions.question: You mix solutions of lead(II) nitrate (Pb(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>) and potassium iodide (KI). A precipitate of PbI<sub>2</sub> forms. Which ions are the spectator ions?
Write the reaction equation for the formation of the precipitate lead(II) iodide from ions.
You mix silver nitrate and sodium chloride. What is the reaction equation of the precipitate that forms?
You mix barium chloride (BaCl<sub>2</sub>) and sodium sulfate (Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>). Which precipitate forms?
Write the full reaction equation for mixing BaCl<sub>2</sub> (aq) and Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (aq).
Write the reaction equation for the formation of the precipitate calcium carbonate from ions.
Which ions make water hard?
What does limescale in a kettle consist of?
You add soda (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>) to hard water. What happens to the Ca<sup>2+</sup> ions?

answers.a: They are converted into Na<sup>+</sup> ions and gas
answers.b: They form a precipitate of CaCO<sub>3</sub> with CO<sub>3</sub><sup>2−</sup> and are removed from the water

questions.question: How can you remove Pb<sup>2+</sup> ions from waste water?

answers.a: Dilute the waste water with a lot of water
answers.b: Boil the water until the salt evaporates
answers.c: Discharge the waste water into the river
answers.d: Add a solution that forms a poorly soluble lead salt, and then filter

questions.question: Which reaction equation describes the removal of Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions with limewater (OH<sup>−</sup> ions)?
Why can you not remove nitrate ions (NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>) from water as a precipitate?

answers.d: Nitrates are very soluble, so a precipitate never forms

questions.question: How do you detect chloride ions in a solution?

answers.a: You boil the solution; salt is formed
answers.b: You add sodium hydroxide solution; the solution turns blue
answers.c: You add hydrochloric acid; a gas is formed
answers.d: You add silver nitrate; a white precipitate of AgCl forms

questions.question: How do you detect sulfate ions in a solution?

answers.a: You measure the pH; it is 7
answers.b: You add silver nitrate; a yellow gas is formed
answers.c: You add limewater; it turns cloudy
answers.d: You add barium chloride; a white precipitate of BaSO<sub>4</sub> forms

questions.question: How do you detect carbon dioxide, and which reaction takes place?
Which two solutions do you mix to make the poorly soluble salt silver chloride?
How do you separate the precipitate from the solution?

answers.a: By filtering; the precipitate stays behind as the residue
answers.c: By distilling; the precipitate is the distillate

questions.question: How do you get the dissolved salt (with the spectator ions) back from the filtrate?

answers.c: By cooling the filtrate to a gas
answers.d: By filtering the filtrate once more

questions.question: You mix solutions of sodium sulfate and potassium nitrate. Does a precipitate form?

answers.d: No, all possible salts dissolve well

questions.question: Write the full reaction equation for mixing Pb(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub> (aq) and KI (aq).
What is the formula of the salt that consists of Ca<sup>2+</sup> and PO<sub>4</sub><sup>3−</sup> ions?
Write the reaction equation for dissolving calcium chloride in water.
Write the reaction equation for dissolving aluminium sulfate (Al<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>) in water.
Write the reaction equation for dissolving sodium carbonate in water.
How many ions form when one formula unit of CaCl<sub>2</sub> dissolves?
How can you see in a reaction equation that a precipitate forms?

answers.a: The formula of the substance is followed by (s), for example AgCl (s)
answers.b: The formula of the substance is followed by (g)
answers.c: The formula of the substance is followed by (aq)
